title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
alternate_titles: Guns, Germs and Steel: A Short History of Everybody for the Last 13,000 Years

contents: Prologue: Yali's question and the proposed environmental answer
Part One, From Eden to Cajamarca: different starting trajectories, Polynesia as comparison, and Pizarro's capture of Atahuallpa
Part Two, The Rise and Spread of Food Production: domesticable species, independent origins, diffusion and continental axes
Part Three, From Food to Guns, Germs, and Steel: disease, writing, technology and political organisation as downstream effects
Part Four, Around the World: applications to Australia and New Guinea, East Asia, Austronesian expansion, the Americas and Africa
Epilogue: the proposal to study long-run history as a science

audiences: Readers asking why power and material development diverged across continents
Readers of big-history synthesis who want explicit causal mechanisms
Students entering debates about geography, culture and institutions
Readers who want an environmental alternative to racial explanations of conquest

sources.title: The 1998 Pulitzer Prize Winner in General Nonfiction
sources.supports: Prize identity, title, author, publisher, 1997 copyright, stated core argument and contemporary author biography.

sources.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
sources.supports: Release date, ISBN, an independent outline of the biogeographic case, praise for its synthesis and anti-racist conclusion, and criticism of prose and redundancy.
sources.limitations: Short contemporary trade review; its displayed page count conflicts with the Norton/Google Books record and is not used.

sources.title: History Upside Down
sources.author_or_publisher: William H. McNeill, The New York Review of Books
sources.supports: A world historian's balanced assessment: praise for the fresh biogeographic angle and axis mechanism, alongside criticism that recorded cultural history is reduced to inadequate natural processes.

sources.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel — author reply and reviewer response
sources.author_or_publisher: Jared Diamond and William H. McNeill, The New York Review of Books
sources.supports: Diamond's stated continental, 13,000-year scope and anti-racist purpose, and McNeill's direct rebuttal concerning culture's capacity to alter environmental constraints.
sources.limitations: A short adversarial exchange, not a systematic evidence review.

sources.title: Geography is not destiny: A quantitative test of Diamond's axis of orientation hypothesis
sources.supports: A direct quantitative test finding scarce prior evidence and challenging the strong form of continental-axis determinism while discussing qualified diffusion patterns.
sources.limitations: Tests one central mechanism with proxy measures; it does not evaluate the whole book.

sources.title: Biogeography and Long-Run Economic Development
sources.author_or_publisher: Ola Olsson and Douglas A. Hibbs Jr., European Economic Review
sources.supports: A formal model and cross-country evidence supporting durable links from initial geography and biogeography through agriculture and later development.
sources.limitations: One empirical extension of Diamond; observational long-run relationships do not settle every causal route.

sources.title: Reversal of Fortune: Geography and Institutions in the Making of the Modern World Income Distribution
sources.author_or_publisher: Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James A. Robinson, Quarterly Journal of Economics
sources.supports: Evidence that institutional reversals among former colonies are central to modern income differences and cannot be explained by a simple time-invariant geography account.
sources.limitations: Addresses modern comparative development rather than directly testing Diamond's prehistoric continental explanation.

sources.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel by Jared Diamond
sources.author_or_publisher: Joseph Fail Jr., Evolution: Education and Outreach
sources.supports: Praise for the book's accessible teaching of ecology, evolution, germs and regional application, together with criticism that the central lesson is repeatedly delivered across more than 400 pages.
sources.limitations: A short ecology-education review, not a historian's audit.

sources.title: Environmentalism and Eurocentrism: A Review Essay
sources.supports: A geographer's direct criticism of environmental determinism, diffusion claims and Eurocentric treatment of innovations.
sources.limitations: A strongly polemical review representing one academic critic; use alongside McNeill and empirical work, not as consensus.

sources.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel by Jared Diamond: Against History
sources.supports: An anthropologist's direct criticism that the framework reduces European domination to distant accidents and underweights political decisions, Indigenous alliances and human agency.
sources.limitations: A forceful teaching essay rather than peer-reviewed research; use as a named agency critique alongside McNeill, Blaut and empirical studies.

workflow.coverage_notes: Structure and claims checked against authorised contents and edition records; purpose checked in Diamond's direct reply; assessment triangulated across contemporary history and ecology reviews plus later empirical work supporting and challenging the biogeographic framework.
